name: Ortur Laser Master H10
tagline: Ortur's enclosed-style H-series: faster frame, tighter integration than LM3
tldr: The H10 is Ortur's step up from the open-frame LM3 line: a more integrated chassis with up to 20W diode power and higher advertised traverse speeds. Still diode-class cutting limits, but a solid pick if you want Ortur ecosystem with a more polished frame.
mainObjective: Integrated Ortur diode for faster engraving and cleaner setup than LM3

priceRange.note: Ortur sells the H10 with 10W or 20W modules only

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

pros: Higher speed potential on optimized jobs
Large Ortur community and firmware support
Competitive price vs xTool D1 Pro
cons: Still open frame: eye protection required
No official 40W option: Ortur lists its LU3-40A module for the LM3 and F10, not the H10
Less proven long-term than LM3 community volume
Not a CO₂ replacement for acrylic shops
beginnerNotes: Choose H10 over LM3 if you want a slightly more modern Ortur platform and can spend a bit more. For maximum community tutorials, LM3 still wins.
proTips: Start with 20W unless you only engrave: Ortur sells the H10 with 10W or 20W modules only, and the 20W ships with a free air pump. Pair with Ortur air assist early for cleaner edges.
primaryUse: Integrated open-frame Ortur diode for faster engraving and moderate thin-wood cutting.
